title: Understand Rates and Unit Rates
objective: I can describe a rate using its two different units and use a model to find a travel time, and I can find a unit rate to compare prices and decide the better buy.
model: unit rate as equal groups (one per item) and a double number line for a constant rate such as travel time

widgets.root: Recomputed $0.50, 30, $0.75 and '12 miles per 1 hour'.

widgets.component: cost per game for Deals B and C
widgets.root: Cells $0.75 and $0.60 per game are numeric; the grader reads the leading number so '$0.75 per game' and '0.75' both pass.

widgets.component: student writes $1.05 for $6.00 ÷ 4
widgets.root: The flagged step 'Set up the division' prints the correct $6.00 ÷ 4 = $1.50 and the wrong $1.05 in the same sentence, so the step the key marks wrong also states the right answer; the slip is a digit transposition, not a rate misconception.
widgets.replacement: Rebuild as a three-step item with an operation error: Read: '$6.00 for 4 games; find the cost of one game.' Set up: 'Divide games by cost: 4 ÷ 6 ≈ 0.67' (flagged); State: 'Each game costs $0.67.' Fix: cost per game means dollars ÷ games, $6.00 ÷ 4 = $1.50.

widgets.where: Practice §5 items 5.1-5.3 (mc, small bag / large bag)
widgets.component: mastery items whose scenario was dropped
widgets.root: 'What is the unit rate for the small bag?', '… for the large bag?' and 'Which size is the better deal?' contain no prices or cups: the bags (3 cups for $2.25; 8 cups for $5.60) exist only in the config scenario, so the items cannot be answered (the choices happen to reveal $2.25 and $5.60 in 5.3).
widgets.replacement: Restate the scenario in each stem: 'The snack bar sells a small bag with 3 cups of popcorn for $2.25 and a large bag with 8 cups for $5.60.' then ask for the small bag unit rate ($0.75 per cup), the large bag ($0.70 per cup) and the better deal (large, $0.70 < $0.75).

widgets.component: 'Which unit rate means the best buy when you compare two token packs?'
widgets.root: A vocabulary-recall question with a self-evident answer ('the lowest cost per token'): it does not make the student compute or compare.
widgets.replacement: Replace with a computed comparison: 'Pack A is 12 tokens for $3.00, Pack B is 20 tokens for $4.60. Which is the better buy, and what is the cost of one token in each?' with choices that include the total-price and the more-tokens traps.

widgets.where: Challenge §2 item 2.5 (num, double number line 150 miles per hour)
widgets.component: double number line with miles 0, 150, 300, 450, 525 above hours 0, 1, 2, 3, ?
widgets.root: The dnl renderer spaces ticks by index, not by value: the gap 450 to 525 (75 miles, half an hour) is drawn as wide as 300 to 450 (150 miles, one hour), so the figure shows 525 miles at 4 hours; the model is also read-only.
widgets.replacement: Make the renderer in assets/studio-viz-model.js place ticks at value / maxValue of the line width (zero aligned on both lines), or throw RangeError when intervals are uneven. Data-only fix: ask for 600 miles with miles [0,150,300,450,600] and hours [0,1,2,3,?] (answer 4), and add one item with a deliberate half-step drawn at half width (0,150,300,450,525 → hours 0,1,2,3,3.5).
